tokens.source: NOT MEASURED — the builder cannot see the orchestrator's usage counter and this dispatch was not launched through factory_dispatch. Recorded as 0 rather than null so gen_paper_table stays runnable; EXCLUDE this row from any token aggregate. The four prior dispatches against the same wall are costed on GRUCellBlock.factory.json.

notes: THE EXAMPLE, finally shipped end to end. The GRU modulation-classifier chain (7 blocks, 65 block cells, 10 nets) had never routed on one 10x12 across four dispatches and ~8200 measured layouts; the best result was ALWAYS exactly one failing net, with WHICH net failed rotating as blocks moved (a saturated array, not a bad anchor). It now routes, builds at 102/120 (65 block + 37 corridor), and classifies the shipped stimulus on the real placed+routed bitstream at agreement 1.000000 against the offline chip-exact golden, segment votes [0,1,2,3], on-chip per-step accuracy ssb 1.000 / bpsk 0.811 / fsk4 0.856 / noise 1.000 asserted EQUAL to the offline model's on the same clip. THE FIX WAS ONE METHOD ON GRUCellBlock: re-fold WIDE-FLAT (10 wide x 5 tall closed row-comb ring + a 1-row egress relay = 10x6) under the CHIP_SCALE placement class. WHY THE PRIOR DIAGNOSIS MISSED IT (the durable lesson, now INV-38): the previous dispatch correctly ruled out capacity, the hop ceiling and the arm size, then argued no fold could close it from a SOUND structural fact - a closed ring can never contain a free through-channel, so all its free space is perimeter and free-space QUALITY measured identical across every legal fold. True, but the conclusion silently inherited INV-9's <=8-across cap, under which a 51-cell block has only THREE bounding boxes. Waive the cap per class and the perimeter of a 10-wide block IS six contiguous full-width rows - the through-channel the ten nets could never find. When a proof says 'no X can do Y', check what quantified the space of X. THE TRADE IS MANDATORY: at full width nothing can reach the block's far side, so its input and output must share ONE edge (fin and oout three cells apart on the north edge, facing the chip's two row-0 ports); asserted in the suite, with a test that DEMONSTRATES the rotated image is unusable rather than narrating it. MEASUREMENT TRAP recorded: the wide fold is NOT cheaper for its own corridors at the anchor the example uses - 58 cells (block + both corridors) at its best anchor vs 64 for the 8x7, but 70 at row 6, where the example seats it to give the front end the port-side rows. A gate measuring only the block's port cost at the example's anchor reads that as a regression and is right about the number, wrong about the outcome; the figure that settles a fold is the WHOLE CHAIN's. BEHAVIOUR PRESERVED EXACTLY: all 49 test_gru_cell.py gates green, 36000 on-chip steps at agreement 1.000000, clip vote 0.9667 on-chip == 0.9667 offline over 120 held-out clips. All three is_face constants MOVED (fin LOCK_FACE 2->1, amx faces (2,3)->(3,2)) and followed automatically because INV-37 had already made them derived - which is exactly why a re-fold this large cost one method instead of a debug cycle. THE EXAMPLE'S OWN REAL BUG was in the DRIVER, not the chip: with the chain routed the first end-to-end run classified 9/12 instead of exactly. in_re and in_im share ONE corridor ending at a BROKER one cell short of the power cell, and in_re's landing carries BOTH staging registers in its data_addrs while in_im's describes the FINAL destination; driving them as two independent deliveries wrote Im into the power cell's Re register, so im stayed 0, power silently became re^2, and every downstream stage still looked individually correct. A complex consumer fed from a port must be driven at the BROKER landing. Now an on-chip mutation gate. COVERAGE HOLE CLOSED: a chip-scale block cannot run the shared full-D4 sweep, so it is gated on its DECLARED CHIP_SCALE_ORIENTATIONS in its own suite (the FFT32 pattern) - which leaves it gated NOWHERE if someone drops it from both places while every suite stays green. New test_chip_scale_blocks_are_gated_elsewhere.py requires every chip-scale class to name its gating suite or be listed as quarantined, and fails a quarantined one that reaches manifest-done. SHIPS: .kyt (hand-placed; a 400-layout search found exactly ONE arrangement that routes AND builds, so open the .kyt, do not import the .grc - the FSK4/QAM16 convention) + .grc (opens/generates/instantiates under the real GRC compiler, server_port 58950, scopes sized below the burst so they paint) + golden + build_kyt.py + demo + README + a self-contained kyttar.gru_demo_stim asserted to produce a clip identical to gru_stimulus.py. 34 example gates, 7 mutations proven to fail (4 offline, 3 on-chip), including a gate that loads the shipped .kyt FROM DISK, builds it and reproduces the golden (the file is what a user opens). ROUTE-QUALITY COST recorded: the ratchet failed the new .kyt at +6 total excess and both detours are a direct consequence of the fold - with the GRU holding rows 6-11 across the full width the front end is confined to rows 1-4, so pow_mean rounds the boxcar footprint (+2) and root_decim drops to the free row 5 to get past the sqrt/boxcar wall (+4); pinned consciously with that explanation. Buying a contiguous through-channel for the big block spends some of the small blocks' lane freedom. SCOPE NOTE: this dispatch was originally tasked to build a fused FeatureExtractorBlock (14 cells, absorbing six front-end blocks to delete six of the ten nets, estimated ~99/120). It was designed and then abandoned UNBUILT when a mid-task course correction relaxed the width cap and the wide fold routed the ORIGINAL six-block chain at 102/120 - the cheaper lever. The net-count arithmetic behind the fused block remains sound and is recorded in the lessons log for a future saturated chain. NOT VERIFIED, stated explicitly: the .grc is gated by test_examples_grc_instantiate (opens, GRC-generates, instantiates) but has NOT been run against a live hosted server the way the transceivers are by test_examples_grc_userpath, and nobody has watched the scopes paint. The end-to-end evidence is the headless on-chip run through the real built bitstream.
